bullets.title: S&P +1.9%, VIX spikes to 20.79 — market up but fear re-emerging
bullets.body: S&P 500 rallied 1.9% to 7,519.56 by mid-morning, yet VIX jumped 18.9% to 20.79 — a divergence suggesting the relief rally is fragile. Pre-market futures were up ~0.9%, with the 10-year yield ticking to 4.84%. Broad tech names led: META +2.9%, AMZN +3.2%, AVGO +3.0%, ANET +3.1%.

bullets.title: NVDA -5.6% on CEO Jensen Huang spy probe — key-man risk front and center
bullets.body: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with a woman identified as a Chinese intelligence asset (Megaspeed International); the Commerce Dept. probe was transferred to DoJ after Nvidia's GC inquired. The board found no evidence of IP compromise and expressed confidence in Huang remaining CEO, but the stock fell ~$9.85 (5.6%) to $176.79. Congressional pressure is building (House Republicans called for a briefing), Polymarket pricing 17% odds Huang exits by Dec 31, and analysts flagged the absence of a clear succession plan as incremental risk.

bullets.title: Citi tactically downgrades US/Global/EU Tech to Neutral — wants cleaner sentiment first
bullets.body: Citi's Global Equity Strategy cut US, Global, and EU Tech from Overweight to Neutral, citing positioning risks and a desire for sentiment to clear before re-rating. The move comes alongside the NVDA CEO overhang and broader L/S deleveraging that pushed Tech net allocation to 14.4% (1st percentile over 1 and 3 years) — from crowded to light.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley 'Buy the Drop' in AI post-midterms — capex cycle elongates, not derails
bullets.body: MS argues the market overreacted to midterm results: ~20% of US data center projects shift from 2028 to 2029 (5GW), but aggregate hyperscaler capex forecasts are unchanged at $1.6T/$1.8T in 2027/2028. A >30% powered data center shortfall persists through 2028; 2029 US growth is expected +38% YoY as delayed projects come online. MS recommends selective 'Buy the Drop' across hyperscalers (AMZN, META, GOOGL, MSFT), powered shell providers less exposed to Texas (WULF, HUT), power/IPPs (BE, SEI, CEG, TLN), and semis (NVDA, AVGO, STX, WDC, LITE, COHR, ANET).

bullets.title: MS sees correction in 'final phase' — S&P targeting 7,100–7,300 retest before year-end rally
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's equity strategy characterizes the selloff as entering its final phase, with S&P targeting 7,100–7,300 as the retest level. SPX forward P/E contracted to ~18x (~16-17x equal-weight), near Liberation Day valuation levels. Tech forward P/E fell to 17.3x vs. a 25-year average of 20x — lowest since March 2020. Macro systematic strategies are expected to sell another $30–40B over the next week, but the largest L/S de-grossing on record (>10% active GMV reduction July–October) and corporate buybacks at ~$5B/day with 90% of S&P in open window provide technical support.

bullets.title: Macro regime shift toward 'Quad 4' (falling growth + inflation) — worst setup for equities
bullets.body: Oppenheimer macro framework flags curve flattening and declining global excess liquidity as signals of a regime shift to Quad 4 — historically the worst setup for stocks. SPX gamma is negative across strikes; 7,200 is the washout level and 7,500 is resistance. GS models project ~$28B in S&P sales next week from vol-control and CTA flows. L/S deleveraging has been severe (gross leverage at 26th percentile, net at 1st), which should limit further forced-selling acceleration.

bullets.title: Fed on track for December rate hike; 10Y at 4.83% — October jobs data cited as catalyst
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and multiple strategists note the October employment report was solid enough to put the Fed on track for a December rate hike. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.83–4.84%, with markets pricing ~80% probability of a December hike but only 43bp of cumulative hikes through end of next year. JPM rates strategy holds a neutral-to-bearish outlook on Treasury futures calendar spreads, with TY most bearish due to historic asset manager net long positioning.

bullets.title: HBM/DRAM super-cycle intact: SK Hynix 60%+ HBM4 yields, shortages through 2027, Q1'27 price hike expected
bullets.body: The DRAM market has entered a ~$200B super-cycle: SK Hynix achieved mid-60% yields on HBM4 (industry high), Samsung is adding HBM base die production for AMD and NVDA at its Texas fab, and spot prices carry 30–50% premiums with shortages expected to persist until new fabs come online in 2028. Analysts warn of a Q1 2027 price hike; GPU rental prices are also firming (B300 +14.46% M/M, B200 +15.35% M/M).

bullets.title: Taiwan Oct exports +58.9% YoY — AI chip boom driving record shipments
bullets.body: Taiwan's October exports jumped 10.8% M/M to a record $94B, up 58.9% YoY vs. 51% consensus, with electronic IC exports up 58.8% YoY and ICT products up 68.3% YoY to all-time highs. The TAIEX bounced 5% on the data but remains -16% from its October peak. TSMC October revenues are due this week as the next global tech momentum read.

bullets.title: Semiconductor export controls tightening — MATCH/AI OVERWATCH Acts pose China chip supply risk
bullets.body: 22V Research sees higher probability of tighter export controls via the MATCH Act and AI OVERWATCH Act, limiting NVDA and chip-equipment suppliers' China sales. The Trump-Xi meeting on Nov 18–19 is flagged as both a catalyst and a risk for Chinese rare-earth retaliation. The NVDA CEO probe will likely heighten Congressional scrutiny on AI chip export enforcement.

bullets.title: AI capex now debt-financed at scale — global credit dynamics shifting, quality divide widening
bullets.body: J.P. Morgan's APAC strategist notes AI-related capex is projected to rise from ~$900B to $1.5T, with an increasing share debt-financed, prompting government pushback in Thailand and Australia. Memory chips now represent ~50% of data center spending. Goldman Sachs is hosting a Nov 16 webinar on how record hyperscaler debt issuance is reshaping EM credit supply/demand dynamics. Post-midterms, financing scrutiny has deepened with a widening quality divide for new construction.

bullets.title: Data center backlash spreading globally — Norway halts reservations, Australia drafting rules, community pushback in Texas/Sydney
bullets.body: Real estate pre-market notes flag growing anti-data center sentiment: Norway halted new electricity reservations until August 2027, Australia is drafting renewable energy requirements, and Stockland scrapped Sydney DC plans after community opposition. In Texas, NextDC is halting uncontracted projects and CRWV is engaging the Texas Governor-elect. Trump supports energy infrastructure permitting legislation, with a Bipartisan Affordability and Jobs Act procedural vote today.

bullets.title: CRWV earnings this week — key read for AI infrastructure stabilization
bullets.body: 22V Research and multiple strategists flag CRWV's upcoming earnings as the pivotal event to stabilize AI-related names. Key metrics to watch: revenue per MW and the 2027 funding path. CRWV is down 49.4% over the past month on 'doom cycle' credit risk concerns and was -1.7%/-2.6% in pre-market.

bullets.title: AMD upgraded to Outperform by Oppenheimer ($600 PT) — benefits from NVDA distraction
bullets.body: Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform with a $600 PT, citing NVDA distraction and Intel CPU weakness as near-term tailwinds. AMD was up 4.1% in pre-market. RBC also highlighted AMD as benefiting from NVDA-related read-throughs, while Klein's note flagged AMD at $450 as attractive given the current overhang on NVDA.

bullets.title: Senator Warren 'ready to go' on 10% credit card rate cap — bearish for card issuers, differentiated for AFRM
bullets.body: Senator Warren, expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, stated she is prepared to work with Trump on capping credit card APRs at 10%, consistent with Trump's January 2026 position. JPM notes AFRM is differentiated by 0% financing structures, no late fees, and ~$250 average transaction size; October volume reaccelerated to high-30% growth after a timing-related Q1 slowdown.

bullets.title: Fed study: oil prices have limited core inflation impact so far, but 25bp upside risk if sustained
bullets.body: A new Fed study finds higher oil prices have not materially raised core inflation to date — undermining the narrative that recent core CPI upticks are energy-driven. However, in a scenario where oil prices remain elevated longer than expected, the model shows a ~25bp gap vs. the no-shock baseline by mid-November. MS Consumer desk expects October core CPI at 0.19% M/M, down from 0.33% in September.

bullets.title: Broad buyback/dividend activity robust — $25B Lam Research, $6B 3M, $5B Marathon authorized week of Nov 2
bullets.body: StreetAccount weekly summary shows 43 dividend increases vs. 2 cuts and 63 new/increased share repurchase authorizations. Major tech authorizations include Lam Research ($25B), AppLovin, and Fabrinet. Corporate buybacks are running at ~$5B/day with 90% of the S&P 500 in an open repurchase window on Monday, providing a technical bid.

bullets.title: Asia AI capex capturing 20GW spillover from US delays — North Asian semis/memory key beneficiaries
bullets.body: J.P. Morgan's APAC CEO podcast and Morgan Stanley both note Asia (Gulf Developments, Keppel, Adani Power, Yangtze Power, Korea/Taiwan chip suppliers) is positioned to capture a material share of data center investment displaced from the US. AI-related companies represent ~50% of regional equity indices and over 70% of Asia earnings growth. Memory chips are now nearly 50% of data center spending, directly benefiting Korean and Taiwanese suppliers.

bullets.title: GOOGL +2.5–3% on new TPU chip acceleration — four specialized SKUs in 2026 addressing AI agent security
bullets.body: Google is accelerating its TPU chip release cadence with four specialized SKUs launching in 2026, targeting confidential computing and AI agent security workloads. The 8tx pairs with AMD CPUs; the 8i Max doubles compute density. The stock was up 2.5–3% in pre-market, partly recovering from AI-sector pressure.

bullets.title: DKNG downgraded by Stifel, UBS, JPM after Q3 miss — PT cut to $22, profitability deferred to 2028
bullets.body: DraftKings was downgraded by Stifel, UBS, and JPMorgan following a Q3 miss and guidance well below Street for Q4 2026 and FY2027 due to a significant increase in Prophet platform investment. The path to profitability is now deferred to 2028. NFL Week 9 added pressure: 93% favorite win rate (13/14 favs won, all 5 biggest spreads covered), pointing to a likely low-hold week — a historically unusual outcome (75%+ fav win rate occurs only ~4.6 weeks per season).
